items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: You mentioned The Last Hurrah, about Curley. And all the interviews with John Ford, he said, “I make Westerns. What’s the big deal?” But Ford is a major American director, and you’re a major American writer and thinker, so nonetheless you were in that position at that time.

I tell you: there were a couple of times when I felt that I had been – I was in a mythological world. Benny Goodman called me up once. I’d never met him. He said, “I’m looking for a tenor player. Who do you think I . . .?” My goodness, Benny Goodman’s asking me? So I said, “Zoot Sims.”
As the editor of Down Beat, can you describe the duties and responsibilities that you took over from Leonard Feather?
